subject: Need direction to create TodoMVC using Shiny

messages.author: cdd33ea759ba3477
messages.subject: Need direction to create TodoMVC using Shiny
parts:
Hi Shiny,

I'm wrestling with how to work my app needs into Shiny's reactive model. I'm trying to create UI elements based on user generated data and then use these inputs as reactive data.

A simple way to illustrate the need is the TodoMVC app (http://todomvc.com/ for example the react.js version is here http://todomvc.com/architecture-examples/react/#/). There are two problems tripping me up right now:

  1. The first is using browser side events to trigger a reactive update. I've seen the action button and that's kind of what I'm looking for but different. In the todoMVC example, instead of pressing the action button, they update on the user hitting the return/enter key. Can this be replicated in Shiny?
  2. The larger problem is dynamically creating UI elements and then using them as reactive data. In the todoMVC example, users create new todo items and then the items become a) editable and b) input for further functionality

Here's a start on the code. With Shiny's reactive model I can only think of how to use it with a static UI, can you point me in the right direction to create and use a dynamic ui?
shiny::runGitHub("renderui", "NoahMarconi")

The todoMVC example illustrates my problem but my use case is user imported data and user defined data manipulation (e.g. like slideware where the number of slides are determined by the user and for each slide the user can edit what's displayed using renderUI elements)

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Need direction to create TodoMVC using Shiny
parts:
I found this pretty interesting so I went ahead and tried it myself. I didn't spend any time polishing the UI but it has the close to the same functionality as the TodoMVC as far as I can tell.

https://github.com/jcheng5/shiny-todo
shiny::runGitHub("shiny-todo", "jcheng5")

One thing I didn't do is the "double-click to edit"--I just rendered them as text boxes all the time. If you wanted to add that functionality you'd do it by implementing a custom input control/binding, just like I had to implement commandInput in the example because "textbox that only sends when you hit Enter" doesn't exist in Shiny.
